scMINER Viewer Guide scMINER Team 2026-05-15 Welcome scMINER Viewer is a pair of sibling packages — one R, one Python — for browsing scMINER single-cell studies offline, with no Java services, no graph database, and no SQL backing. Package Language Path Role scminerViewer R scminerViewer/ Prepare scMINER studies (write graph-import layout + .scminer.h5 bundle); serve a Shiny app and the multi-study browser. scminer_viewer Python scminer_viewer/ Read the same .scminer.h5 bundle; serve a Shiny-for-Python single-study viewer and multi-study browser. How to read this guide Chapter 1 — high-level architecture: bundle format, shard tree, multi-study layout, lazy-mode contract. Chapter 2 — installation in shell, R, RStudio, and Python. Chapter 3 — end-to-end tutorial: prepare a study, build a bundle, serve it, add a second study, browse them. Chapter 4 — full schema of the prepare_study() YAML config. Chapter 5 — deep-dive on the .scminer.h5 bundle and the sharded matrix tree. Chapter 6 — R API reference (orchestrators, staged helpers, bundle + Shiny entry points). Chapter 7 — Python API reference (Study dataclass, lazy gene_values, browser). Chapter 8 — Shiny app walkthrough: every panel, every tab, every control. Chapter 9 — troubleshooting: lazy-load corruption, shard_dir mismatches, missing genes, etc. Lazy by design (TL;DR) Each study lives in its own subfolder under a shared root: data/ ├── 2327/ <- one studyID per folder │ ├── 2327.scminer.h5 <- ~80 MB bundle (metadata + indexes) │ ├── Cell/, Gene/, Network_*/, study_meta/, study_gene_*/ │ ├── expression_files/2327/<letter>/<gene>.csv.gz │ └── activity_files/2327/{meta.csv, TF/, SIG/} ├── 9999/ │ └── ... At app startup, only the bundle is read. When the user picks a gene, exactly one <gene>.csv.gz is decompressed and cached. The Heatmap, Bubble, Feature, and Violin tabs all use this lazy accessor; the Cluster Plot and the Clusters table need no shard reads at all. run_browser(root_dir) scans the root and presents every study as a card; clicking a card opens that study’s viewer.

Chapter 1 Overview Two packages, one bundle format Design decisions (locked) What’s in scope Repository layout

Chapter 1 Overview Two packages, one bundle format scMINER Viewer is intentionally split into two co-equal packages so that: the R package owns data preparation (writing the bundle + graph layout) plus a Shiny single-study viewer and the multi-study browser; the Python package owns a Shiny-for-Python viewer + multi-study browser that consumes the same .scminer.h5 bundle. The shared contract is a single HDF5 file — <studyID>.scminer.h5 — written by R and read by either package. Every other feature lives on top of this contract. Design decisions (locked) Question Choice Why Backend Standalone, file-based No Java services, no graph DB, no MySQL. Drop a study tree on disk and either package can render it. Storage HDF5 bundle alongside the graph-import shard tree One file the apps load in one shot; preserves compatibility with the original Neo4j-import pipeline. Lazy values Bundle stores indexes only (which genes have shards); matrix values stay on disk Bundles stay ~80 MB even when matrices are hundreds of MB. The app reads exactly one shard per gene-selection event. Multi-study One subfolder per study under a shared root prepare_study() writes to <root>/<studyID>/...; run_browser(root) discovers every study. UI tabs Six core panels (Cluster / Heatmap / Bubble / Feature / Violin / Network) with nested per-gene → per-cell-type → per-relationship pickers Mirrors the layout at https://scminer.stjude.org/study/Tregs. Python UI framework Shiny for Python Same reactive model as R Shiny; minimises divergence between the two packages. What’s in scope Reading scMINER ExpressionSet RDS / activity RDS / networks TSV via prepare_study() (R). Writing the graph-import layout (the existing Neo4j-style TSV + per-gene CSV tree). Writing the lazy-mode .scminer.h5 bundle. Browsing one study at a time via run_app() (R) or scminer-viewer run (Python). Browsing many studies under a root via run_browser() (R) or scminer-viewer browse (Python). Cluster table with checkbox selection, color swatches, and live-updating per-cluster cell counts that respond to the Sampling % control. Downsampling (Sampling %) — auto-applied above 65K cells. Default-gene auto-load on app startup (mirrors the Vue portal’s preGenes). Heatmap diverging blue-white-red palette. 3-level nested viewer tabs (Gene → CellType → Expression/TF/SIG) for the Feature, Violin, and Network panels. Repository layout scMINER-Viewer/ ├── IMPLEMENTATION.md architecture & status doc ├── README.md top-level entry point ├── book/ this guide (bookdown) ├── data/ multi-study root │ └── 2327/ │ ├── 2327.scminer.h5 │ ├── Cell/, Gene/, Network_*/ │ ├── study_meta/, study_gene_*/ │ ├── expression_files/2327/ │ └── activity_files/2327/ ├── scminerViewer/ R package │ ├── R/, tests/ │ ├── inst/extdata/example_config.yml │ └── inst/scripts/build_2327_bundle.R └── scminer_viewer/ Python package └── src/scminer_viewer/{data,app,browser,cli}.py + plots/ Continue to Chapter 2 for setup, or jump to Chapter 3 for the end-to-end walkthrough.

Chapter 2 Installation Requirements R / RStudio Python Common installation issues

Chapter 2 Installation Requirements R ≥ 4.x with hard dependencies: hdf5r, Matrix, methods, data.table, R.utils. Python ≥ 3.9 with hard dependencies: shiny, shinywidgets, h5py, numpy, scipy, pandas, plotly. Optional R Suggests (needed only when you exercise certain code paths): Biobase (Bioconductor) — for ExpressionSet inputs to prepare_study() / prepare_study_from_eset(). yaml — for prepare_study()’s YAML config entry point. shiny, bslib, plotly, DT, visNetwork, htmlwidgets — for the Shiny app. roxygen2 — only needed if you edit source comments and want to regenerate man pages. R / RStudio From the shell R CMD build scminerViewer R CMD INSTALL scminerViewer_0.1.0.tar.gz From R or RStudio # devtools / pak / remotes all work — choose whichever you already have install.packages("devtools") devtools::install("scminerViewer") # run from the project root In RStudio: File → Open Project… and pick scminerViewer/ (it ships a .Rproj). Build → Install Package (Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + B). To install all Suggests too: install.packages(c("yaml", "shiny", "bslib", "plotly", "DT", "visNetwork", "htmlwidgets")) if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager") BiocManager::install("Biobase") Verify library(scminerViewer) ?prepare_study # opens the man page If ?prepare_study returns “No documentation found”, the man pages weren’t generated. From the package source: roxygen2::roxygenise("scminerViewer") # writes NAMESPACE + man/*.Rd then reinstall. Python python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install -e "scminer_viewer[dev]" This installs the runtime deps plus pytest / pytest-cov. The CLI is available as scminer-viewer: scminer-viewer --help Verify: scminer-viewer list data scminer-viewer info data/2327/2327.scminer.h5 Common installation issues 2.0.1 “lazy-load database is corrupt” / “interrupted promise evaluation” R memory-maps the package’s .rdb file during library(). If a second R process reinstalls the package while the first one still has it loaded, the offsets go stale and you’ll see one of: Error: lazy-load database '.../scminerViewer.rdb' is corrupt Warning: restarting interrupted promise evaluation Error in R_decompress1 The cure is always: Quit all R sessions that have the package loaded (Cmd/Ctrl + Q in RStudio; this exits the R process — restarting alone isn’t enough). Wipe the install directory from the shell: rm -rf "$HOME/StJude/Research/R_lib/scMINERViewer/scminerViewer" Reinstall from a fresh R session: .libPaths(c("$HOME/StJude/Research/R_lib/scMINERViewer", .libPaths())) devtools::install("scminerViewer", upgrade = "never") 2.0.2 Missing system libraries on macOS hdf5r needs HDF5; if install.packages("hdf5r") fails, install HDF5 with Homebrew first: brew install hdf5 then retry the R install.

Chapter 3 Tutorial: from zero to a multi-study browser A — Prepare one study from a YAML config B — Migrate an existing on-disk study (no RDS needed) C — Browse one or many studies D — Adding a second study E — Inspect what’s available without launching anything

Chapter 3 Tutorial: from zero to a multi-study browser This chapter walks through the most common workflow end-to-end: prepare one study, browse it, add a second study, browse them together. All paths assume the project root as the working directory. A — Prepare one study from a YAML config # 1) Copy the annotated template that ships with the package file.copy( system.file("extdata", "example_config.yml", package = "scminerViewer"), "config.yml" ) Open config.yml and edit: output: — the root that will host all your studies (e.g. "data"). study.* — ID, abbreviation, titles for this study. input.expression — path to your expression ExpressionSet RDS. input.activity (optional) — path to your activity ExpressionSet. input.networks (optional) — path to the networks TSV. Then: library(scminerViewer) prepare_study("config.yml") This writes data/<studyID>/<studyID>.scminer.h5 plus the full graph layout (Cell/, Gene/, Network_*/, …) and the per-gene shard tree (expression_files/<studyID>/<letter>/<gene>.csv.gz and activity_files/<studyID>/{TF,SIG}/...) into data/<studyID>/. B — Migrate an existing on-disk study (no RDS needed) If you already have the graph-layout TSVs + shard tree on disk (e.g. under data/example/), build the bundle directly without invoking the Biobase pipeline: study <- read_graph_study(data_dir = "data/example", study_id = "2327") dir.create("data/2327", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) write_bundle( bundle_path = "data/2327/2327.scminer.h5", meta = study$meta, cells = study$cells, clusters = study$clusters, genes = study$genes, expression_genes = study$expression_genes, activity_tf_genes = study$activity_tf_genes, activity_sig_genes = study$activity_sig_genes, network_tf = study$network_tf, network_sig = study$network_sig, overwrite = TRUE ) If you also want the shard tree co-located with the new bundle, move it once: mv data/example/expression_files data/2327/ mv data/example/activity_files data/2327/ Otherwise pass shard_dir = to run_app() / run_browser() (see C). C — Browse one or many studies Single study (R) # Bundle and shards co-located (default — auto-discovered) run_app("data/2327/2327.scminer.h5", port = 8000) # Shards live elsewhere run_app("data/2327/2327.scminer.h5", shard_dir = "data/example", port = 8000) Single study (Python) scminer-viewer run data/2327/2327.scminer.h5 --port 8000 scminer-viewer run data/2327/2327.scminer.h5 \ --shard-dir data/example --port 8000 Multi-study browser (R) run_browser("data", port = 8000) # When shards still live in the legacy data/example/ tree run_browser("data", shard_dir = "data/example", port = 8000) Multi-study browser (Python) scminer-viewer browse data --port 8000 scminer-viewer browse data --shard-dir data/example --port 8000 Inside the browser, each study is a card; clicking opens ?study=<sid> (R) or sets a reactive value (Python) to drill in. A “← Back to studies” link returns to the index. D — Adding a second study Point prepare_study() at the same root with a new study.ID. Each call creates a sibling <sid>/ folder: data/ ├── 2327/ # first study │ └── 2327.scminer.h5 └── 9999/ # second study └── 9999.scminer.h5 run_browser("data") (or scminer-viewer browse data) now shows two cards. No rebuild of the existing study is required. E — Inspect what’s available without launching anything discover_studies() returns one row per bundle found under a root: scminerViewer::discover_studies("data") # studyID studyAbbr shortTitle longTitle species n_cells n_genes n_clusters bundle_path study_dir # 1 2327 tex Tex Single-cell RNA-seq … Mus musculus 8464 9861 3 data/2327/2327.scminer.h5 data/2327 scminer-viewer list data # studyID studyAbbr shortTitle species n_cells n_genes n_clusters bundle_path # 2327 tex Tex Mus musculus 8464 9861 3 data/2327/2327.scminer.h5 Useful for sanity-checking your layout before launching a browser session, or for scripting (e.g. iterate over every study’s bundle in a batch job).

Chapter 4 Config YAML reference Full schema Field-by-field Parsing the config without loading the RDS files Auto-generated cluster metadata

Chapter 4 Config YAML reference prepare_study(config_path) is the YAML-driven entry point for the full pipeline. It points at a scMINER ExpressionSet RDS (and optional activity + networks) and writes both the graph-import layout and the lazy-mode bundle in one call. Two examples ship with the project: File Role scminerViewer/inst/extdata/example_config.yml Annotated template — every field documented inline; reachable via system.file(). data/example/2327.yml Concrete runnable config keyed to the actual 2327 study (Tex). Edit input.* paths and run. Copy the template: file.copy( system.file("extdata", "example_config.yml", package = "scminerViewer"), "config.yml" ) Full schema # Where to write everything — the bundle lands at # <output>/<studyID>/<studyID>.scminer.h5 (per-study subfolder). output: data # Study identity study: ID: "2327" studyAbbr: tex longTitle: > Single-cell RNA sequencing of progenitor, intermediate and terminally exhausted CD8+ T cells from tumors and chronic viral infection shortTitle: Tex # Sample-level metadata species: Mus musculus coordinate: UMAP # also the pData column prefix (UMAP_1, UMAP_2) # Cluster colour palette — auto-fills the study_meta.csv `Color` column # and the bundle's clusters/color group. Pass any ggsci palette name: # npg, aaas, lancet, nejm, jama, jco, ucscgb, d3, locuszoom, igv, # uchicago, startrek, tron, futurama, rickandmorty, simpsons # See <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ggsci/vignettes/ggsci.html>. cluster_palette: npg # default — Nature Publishing Group # pData / fData column names in the source ExpressionSet cellID: cellID # rownames are also assigned to this column cellType: cellGroup # the cell-type / cluster label cellGroup: cellGroup # falls back to cellType when omitted geneSymbol: geneSymbol # column in fData carrying the gene symbol # Input files input: expression: inputs/2327_expression.rds # required, Biobase ExpressionSet activity: inputs/2327_activity.rds # optional, ExpressionSet # rows ending in _TF / _SIG split # into the two activity matrices networks: inputs/2327_networks.tsv # optional, tab-separated: # source, target, NetworkType, # CellGroup, mi, pearson, # spearman, rho, pvalue Field-by-field Key Required Default Notes output yes — Root directory for the per-study subfolder. The bundle ends up at <output>/<studyID>/<studyID>.scminer.h5. study.ID yes — Numeric or string. Used as the subfolder name. study.studyAbbr yes — Short identifier (URL slug). study.longTitle yes — Full study description. study.shortTitle yes — One-line label. species no "" e.g. "Mus musculus". Also auto-filled from the manifests if missing. coordinate no "UMAP" Both the meta field and the pData column prefix — <coord>_1 and <coord>_2. cellID no "cellID" pData column carrying the cellID. Rownames are also written into this column. cellType no "cellGroup" pData column carrying the cell-type label. cellGroup no cellType pData column carrying the cell-group label. geneSymbol no "geneSymbol" fData column carrying the gene symbol. cluster_palette no "npg" ggsci palette name for auto-generated cluster colors. One of npg, aaas, lancet, nejm, jama, jco, ucscgb, d3, locuszoom, igv, uchicago, startrek, tron, futurama, rickandmorty, simpsons (see the ggsci vignette). Falls back to a baked-in NPG palette if ggsci isn’t installed. input.expression yes — Path to the expression ExpressionSet RDS. input.activity no none Path to the activity ExpressionSet RDS. Rows ending in _TF / .TF go to activity_tf; _SIG / .SIG go to activity_sig. input.networks no none Path to the networks TSV. Parsing the config without loading the RDS files load_study_config() parses the YAML, validates required keys, and fills in defaults. It does not touch any RDS / TSV files referenced by input.* — useful for sanity-checking the config or building a custom pipeline: cfg <- scminerViewer::load_study_config("config.yml") str(cfg) See Chapter 6 for the full list of staged helpers (load_study_config, extract_cells, extract_genes, extract_expression, extract_activity, read_networks, fill_clusters) that prepare_study() is composed of. Auto-generated cluster metadata prepare_study() always emits a study_meta/<studyID>_study_meta.csv with full color + label-position info, even when your input ExpressionSet only carries cellType (no precomputed cluster table). Two pieces are auto-filled by fill_clusters(): Color — n_clusters colours pulled from the configured ggsci palette (cluster_palette above). Default is NPG (Nature Publishing Group). If ggsci isn’t installed, a baked-in 10-colour NPG fallback is used. Label_1, Label_2 — per-cluster centroids: mean(coord1) and mean(coord2) over the cells in each cluster. The cluster plot uses these to place the cluster-name annotations. Existing values in the clusters data.frame (when one is supplied) are preserved; only NA / empty cells are filled in. So you can hand-pick a few colours and let the rest fall back to ggsci.

Chapter 5 Bundle format & shard tree HDF5 bundle layout (bundleVersion = 1) Shard tree Lazy contract Discovering studies under a multi-study root

Chapter 5 Bundle format & shard tree The .scminer.h5 bundle is the R↔︎Python contract. It’s a small HDF5 file (~80 MB for an 8K-cell study) that contains everything the apps need at startup — except the matrix values, which stay on disk in the shard tree and are read lazily. HDF5 bundle layout (bundleVersion = 1) /meta/ studyID, studyAbbr, longTitle, shortTitle, species, coordinate (string) bundleVersion (int, = 1) /cells/ cellID (N,) string cellType (N,) string cellGroup (N,) string coord1 (N,) float64 coord2 (N,) float64 /clusters/ cellType (K,) string count (K,) int32 color (K,) string (hex) label_1 (K,) float64 optional — x for cluster label placement label_2 (K,) float64 optional — y for cluster label placement /genes/ symbol (G,) string master picker list /index/ optional, "which genes are available" expression (G_e,) string present iff expression shards exist activity_tf (G_t,) string activity_sig (G_s,) string /defaults/ optional, "load these on app startup" genes (D,) string /network_tf/ optional source, target, cellType string mi, pearson, spearman, rho, pvalue float64 /network_sig/ optional, same columns Strings are UTF-8 variable-length. Scalar string datasets are stored as 1-element arrays by the R writer; the Python reader unwraps them automatically. Compatibility rules (both packages MUST honour): Unknown groups → treat as future-bundle-versions; ignore. Any optional group may be absent. Scalar string datasets may be either 1-element arrays or true scalars. Shard tree Sharded by the first lowercase letter of each gene name (or nm for non-alphabetic), with a single cell-ID header per matrix type: <shard_dir>/ ├── expression_files/<studyID>/ │ ├── meta.csv one line, comma-separated cellIDs │ └── <letter>/<gene>.csv.gz gzipped 1-row CSV of N values └── activity_files/<studyID>/ ├── meta.csv shared by TF and SIG (may be a cell subset) ├── TF/<letter>/<gene>.csv.gz └── SIG/<letter>/<gene>.csv.gz <letter> is tolower(substr(gene, 1, 1)) if alphabetic, else nm. Path is derived from the gene name, not the manifest’s File column. Cell-ID column order is read once per matrix type from meta.csv; a permutation index aligns shard columns to cells$cellID, so missing cells become zero columns automatically. The activity meta.csv is shared between TF and SIG and may list a subset of the cells in the expression meta (activity is computed only for cells passing some upstream filter). Lazy contract load_study(bundle_path) reads the bundle and returns a thin handle that knows where the shards are. No matrix values are loaded. gene_values(study, gene, relationship) (R) / study.gene_values(gene, relationship) (Python) reads exactly one shard from disk, caches the aligned vector on the study handle, and returns it. study <- scminerViewer::load_study("data/2327/2327.scminer.h5") vals <- scminerViewer::gene_values(study, "Mrpl15", "Express_normalized") length(vals) # nrow(study$cells) import scminer_viewer study = scminer_viewer.load_study("data/2327/2327.scminer.h5") vals = study.gene_values("Mrpl15", "Express_normalized") vals.shape # (n_cells,) Discovering studies under a multi-study root discover_studies(root_dir) scans for <studyID>/<studyID>.scminer.h5 patterns and returns a row-per-study data frame. Useful for scripting or as the data source for the browser’s card-grid index page. df <- scminerViewer::discover_studies("data") nrow(df) # number of studies the browser will list import scminer_viewer df = scminer_viewer.discover_studies("data") df.shape[0]

Chapter 6 R API reference The R package’s public surface, grouped by role. Orchestrators (one-shot prep) Function Purpose prepare_study(config_path, emit, verbose) YAML-driven entry. Requires yaml + Biobase. prepare_study_from_eset(out_dir, expression_eset, ...) Accepts a Biobase ExpressionSet. Splits activity rows into TF/SIG by _TF/_SIG row suffix. Requires Biobase. prepare_study_data(out_dir, meta, cells, clusters, genes, expression, ..., default_genes, emit, verbose) Lowest-level orchestrator — plain R structures only. All three accept emit = c("graph", "bundle") to skip either output. Staged helpers (granular control / debug) Call these directly when you want to inspect an intermediate before committing to disk. prepare_study() and prepare_study_from_eset() are thin wrappers over them. Function Purpose load_study_config(config_path) Parse + validate the YAML; fill defaults. Pure parsing — does not touch any RDS / TSV files. extract_cells(eset, cell_id_col, cell_type_col, cell_group_col, coordinate_col) pData(eset) → cells data.frame. Errors loudly on missing columns. extract_genes(eset, gene_symbol_col) fData(eset) → character vector of gene symbols. extract_expression(eset, genes = NULL) exprs(eset) → sparse Matrix (genes × cells). Sets rownames from genes if provided. extract_activity(activity_eset, master_genes) Splits rows by _TF/_SIG suffix; returns list(tf, sig) reindexed to master_genes. Either element may be NULL. read_networks(path) Parse a scMINER networks TSV; returns list(tf, sig) data.frames. fill_clusters(cells, clusters = NULL, palette = "npg") Auto-populate a clusters data.frame: counts from table(cells$cellType), colours from any ggsci palette, label positions from mean(coord1) / mean(coord2) per cluster. Existing non-NA values are preserved. Bundle + study handles Function Purpose write_bundle(bundle_path, meta, cells, clusters, genes, expression_genes, activity_tf_genes, activity_sig_genes, default_genes, network_tf, network_sig, overwrite) Write the .scminer.h5 bundle. Indexes + metadata only; values stay on disk. load_study(bundle_path, shard_dir = NULL) Read a .scminer.h5 into an S3 scminer_study list. shard_dir defaults to dirname(bundle_path). gene_values(study, gene, relationship) Lazily read one gene’s row from the shard tree (Express_normalized, Activity_tf, or Activity_sig). Cached on the study handle. read_graph_study(data_dir, study_id) Reconstruct study inputs from the on-disk graph layout. Per-matrix indexes come from the manifest CSVs; shard values are never loaded eagerly. Auto-detects both <data_dir>/Study/<sid>_study.tsv (flat) and <data_dir>/<sid>/Study/... (wrapped) layouts. Shiny entry points Function Purpose run_app(bundle_path, shard_dir = NULL, host, port, launch_browser, ...) Launch the single-study Shiny app. build_app(bundle_path, shard_dir = NULL) Build a single-study shiny.appobj without launching (for tests / embedding). discover_studies(root_dir) Return one row per <studyID>/<studyID>.scminer.h5 found under root_dir. run_browser(root_dir, shard_dir = NULL, host, port, launch_browser, ...) Launch the multi-study browser. Card-grid index; click → ?study=<id> opens the standard viewer with a “← Back” link. build_browser(root_dir, shard_dir = NULL) Build the multi-study shiny.appobj without launching. Debug / granular workflow When something goes wrong with prepare_study(), drive the pipeline manually one step at a time: library(scminerViewer) # 1) Parse the config without touching the RDS files cfg <- load_study_config("config.yml") str(cfg) # see exactly what defaults got applied # 2) Load the inputs (slow — gigabyte-sized RDS files) expr_eset <- readRDS(cfg$input$expression) act_eset <- if (!is.null(cfg$input$activity)) readRDS(cfg$input$activity) # 3) Extract each piece independently — every helper returns a plain # R structure you can print, summary(), or modify cells <- extract_cells( expr_eset, cell_id_col = cfg$cellID, cell_type_col = cfg$cellType, cell_group_col = cfg$cellGroup, coordinate_col = cfg$coordinate ) genes <- extract_genes(expr_eset, gene_symbol_col = cfg$geneSymbol) expr <- extract_expression(expr_eset, genes = genes) act <- if (!is.null(act_eset)) extract_activity(act_eset, genes) else list(tf = NULL, sig = NULL) nets <- if (!is.null(cfg$input$networks)) read_networks(cfg$input$networks) else list(tf = NULL, sig = NULL) # 4) Inspect / tweak before writing head(cells); dim(expr); table(sapply(nets, NROW)) # 5) Hand the parts to prepare_study_data — writes graph + bundle prepare_study_data( out_dir = cfg$output, meta = list(studyID = cfg$study$ID, studyAbbr = cfg$study$studyAbbr, longTitle = cfg$study$longTitle, shortTitle= cfg$study$shortTitle, species = cfg$species, coordinate= cfg$coordinate), cells = cells, genes = genes, expression = expr, activity_tf = act$tf, activity_sig = act$sig, network_tf = nets$tf, network_sig = nets$sig, emit = c("graph", "bundle"), verbose = TRUE )

Chapter 7 Python API reference The Python package exposes the same lazy-mode + multi-study contract as the R package. Single-study and multi-study viewers are both built on top of Study + gene_values(). Public symbols Symbol Purpose load_study(bundle_path, shard_dir=None) -> Study Read a .scminer.h5 into a Study dataclass. shard_dir defaults to Path(bundle_path).parent. Study Dataclass: meta, cells (pandas, indexed by cellID), clusters (pandas, indexed by cellType), genes (numpy), expression_index / activity_tf_index / activity_sig_index (numpy or None), default_genes (numpy or None), network_tf / network_sig (pandas or None), shard_dir. Study.gene_values(gene, relationship) Lazily read one gene’s row from the shard tree; numpy ndarray aligned to Study.cells.index, or None if missing. Cached per gene. Study.has_gene(gene, relationship) True if gene is in the corresponding bundle index. build_app(bundle_path, shard_dir=None) -> shiny.App Build a single-study Shiny app. run_app(bundle_path, shard_dir=None, host, port, launch_browser) Build and serve the single-study Shiny app via uvicorn (blocking). discover_studies(root_dir) -> pandas.DataFrame One row per <studyID>/<studyID>.scminer.h5 under root_dir. build_browser(root_dir, shard_dir=None) -> shiny.App Build a multi-study browser app. run_browser(root_dir, shard_dir=None, host, port, launch_browser) Serve the multi-study browser. Plot helpers Function Purpose plots.cluster_plot(study, active_clusters, dot_size, show_labels, cell_mask) Plotly cluster scatter (coord1 / coord2 colored by cellType). plots.feature_plot(study, gene, relationship, active_clusters, dot_size, cell_mask) Per-cell scatter colored by gene values. plots.violin_plot(study, gene, relationship, active_clusters, cell_mask) Per-cluster violin of gene values. plots.heatmap_plot(study, genes, relationship, active_clusters, cell_mask) Gene × cluster mean heatmap (blue-white-red diverging palette). plots.bubble_plot(study, genes, relationship, active_clusters, cell_mask) Gene × cluster, dot size = pct expressing, color = mean. plots.network_plot(study, gene, network_type, active_clusters) TF/SIG neighbourhood of one gene rendered with networkx spring layout. Every helper accepts an optional cell_mask parameter (boolean ndarray of length n_cells) that intersects with the active_clusters filter — used by the app’s Sampling % control. CLI scminer-viewer info <bundle> [--shard-dir DIR] Print a one-line Study summary. scminer-viewer list <root_dir> Tabular listing of every <sid>/<sid>.scminer.h5 found under <root_dir>. scminer-viewer run <bundle> [options] Launch the single-study Shiny webui. --shard-dir DIR Directory containing the shard tree if not co-located. --host HOST default 127.0.0.1 --port PORT default 8000 --no-browser don't open a browser window scminer-viewer browse <root_dir> [options] Launch the multi-study browser. --shard-dir DIR Override the per-study shard root for every bundle. --host HOST, --port PORT, --no-browser as above. Programmatic example import scminer_viewer # Single study study = scminer_viewer.load_study("data/2327/2327.scminer.h5") print(study) # <Study tex (2327) cells=8464 genes=9861 clusters=3 ...> expr = study.gene_values("Mrpl15", "Express_normalized") print(expr.shape) # (8464,) print((expr != 0).sum()) # number of cells with non-zero expression # Multi-study browser studies = scminer_viewer.discover_studies("data") print(studies[["studyID", "studyAbbr", "n_cells"]]) # Build but don't launch (e.g. for embedding) app = scminer_viewer.build_browser("data") # Launch (blocking) scminer_viewer.run_browser("data", port=8000) Differences vs the R package The Python and R packages are deliberately kept feature-equivalent. A few small differences that arise from the underlying frameworks: Navigation between studies in the browser: R uses URL routing (?study=<sid>); Python uses an in-app reactive value plus a JS-fired Shiny event. Both render the standard single-study viewer with a “← Back to studies” link. Cluster table: R uses a custom HTML <input type="checkbox"> column wired via JS; Python uses render.DataGrid(selection_mode="rows") (clicking a row toggles cluster visibility — functionally the same, visually slightly different). prepare_study() / writing bundles is R-only. Use R to author bundles; use either package to read them.

Chapter 8 Shiny app walkthrough This chapter walks through every panel and control in the single-study viewer. The R and Python apps are visually equivalent; screenshots and labels apply to both. Layout +-----------------------------------------------------------+ | Study title (long title + species + n_cells + n_genes) | +-----------------------------------------------------------+ | Study Info & Controls | Clusters | | - Cells: 8,464/8,464| ☑ TEX_intermediate ▮▮▮ count | | - Coordinate: UMAP | ☑ TEX_progenitor ▮▮ count | | - Dot Size: [4] | ☑ TEX_terminally ▮▮▮▮ count | | - Show Labels: [on] | | | - Sampling %: [100] | | | | | | Gene Selection | | | [Type to add gene(s)…] | | +-----------------------------------------------------------+ | Cluster Plot | Heatmap | Bubble | Feature | Violin | Net.| | | | (active tab content here) | | | +-----------------------------------------------------------+ Study Info & Controls Cells — displayed live as visible / total. Visible cells honour both the cluster table checkboxes and the Sampling %. Coordinate — read-only; shows the coordinate system (e.g. UMAP). Dot Size — affects cluster + feature plots. Show Labels — toggles cluster-name annotations on the cluster plot (positions come from the label_1 / label_2 columns in study$clusters). Sampling % — per-cluster proportional downsampling. The session shuffles each cluster’s cell indices once; the reactive then takes the first pct% from each shuffled vector. Deterministic for a given (cluster, pct) so plots don’t flicker between tabs. Auto-set to floor(65_000 / n_cells * 100) when the study has more than 65K cells. Clusters A 4-column table: Show (checkbox), Cluster, Cells, Color. Show — a per-row HTML <input type="checkbox">. Toggling fires a Shiny event (Shiny.setInputValue('cluster_checkbox', …)) that updates the visible cluster set. The checkbox’s checked attribute is sourced from the server state, so it survives Sampling % changes (no “uncheck → change sampling → all clusters back on” surprise). Cells — visible / total, live-updated by the Sampling % control. Visible counts how many of that cluster’s cells survive the sampling mask; total is the underlying study count from the bundle. Color — the per-cluster swatch (from the bundle’s /clusters/color dataset). Gene Selection Server-side selectizeInput (R) / input_selectize (Python) keyed off the bundle’s genes/symbol master list. Type-ahead is debounced; only the first ~200 matches are sent to the browser per query. If the bundle has a /defaults/genes group, those genes are pre-selected on startup. Genes can be removed with the × button on each chip (R) or by clicking the chip (Python). Plot tabs Cluster Plot A 2D scatter of all cells (after sampling + cluster filter), colored by cellType. Optionally annotated with cluster labels positioned at the label_1 / label_2 coordinates from the bundle. Heatmap Gene × cluster mean of values across each cluster’s sampled cells. Diverging blue-white-red palette (ColorBrewer RdBu reversed, zmid = 0) so positive values lean red and negative (e.g. z-scored activity) lean blue. Bubble Plot Gene × cluster: dot size encodes pct expressing (fraction of cells with non-zero value), dot color encodes the mean. Feature Plot (3-level nested) Feature Plot ├── Gene tab: Mrpl15 │ ├── Cell Type pill: All │ │ └── Card: Expression | TF | SIG (each is a per-cell scatter) │ ├── Cell Type pill: TEX_intermediate │ │ └── Card: Expression | TF | SIG │ ├── Cell Type pill: TEX_progenitor │ │ └── Card: Expression | TF | SIG │ └── Cell Type pill: TEX_terminally │ └── Card: Expression | TF | SIG ├── Gene tab: Stat1 │ └── ... Outermost: per-gene tabs from the gene selectize. Middle: cell-type pills (All + every cluster). All shows the full UMAP coloured by gene value; picking a single cluster shows only those cells. Innermost: a card-pill switcher for Expression / TF / SIG. Violin Plot Same 3-level nesting as Feature Plot. With All selected, every cluster gets its own violin side-by-side; picking a single cluster shows a single violin (useful for comparing Expression vs TF vs SIG within one cluster). Network Same nesting, except the relationship card has only TF / SIG (there is no expression network). Each edge in the bundle is associated with a cellType; selecting a cell-type pill filters the network to just those edges. The network is rendered with visNetwork (R) or networkx + plotly (Python). Up to 60 edges around the focal gene are shown, sorted by |mi|. Multi-study browser run_browser(root_dir) (R) and scminer-viewer browse <root_dir> (Python) render a card-grid index — one card per study found by discover_studies(). Each card shows the shortTitle, studyAbbr, species, n_cells × n_genes × n_clusters, and the longTitle (clamped with a title= hover-tooltip for the full text). Clicking a card opens the standard single-study layout above, with a “← Back to studies” link in the top-left.

Chapter 9 Troubleshooting “lazy-load database is corrupt” / “interrupted promise evaluation” meta.csv not found: data/<sid>/expression_files/<sid>/meta.csv No documentation for 'prepare_study' could not find function "%>%" Plotly “No trace type specified … Setting the mode to markers” run_browser shows no studies A gene I expect is missing from the picker Bundle is huge (>1 GB) A specific cluster disappears with sampling on Error: attempt to construct sparseMatrix with more than 2^31-1 nonzero entries

Chapter 9 Troubleshooting “lazy-load database is corrupt” / “interrupted promise evaluation” R memory-maps the package’s .rdb file during library() and doesn’t release the handle on reinstall. If a second R process reinstalls the package while the first one still has it loaded — or the same session reinstalls itself — you’ll see one of: Error: lazy-load database '.../scminerViewer.rdb' is corrupt Warning: restarting interrupted promise evaluation Error in R_decompress1 The crude fix is the recipe most blogs prescribe: quit every R session holding the package, wipe the install dir, reinstall from a fresh session. Three better options: 1. Don’t library() during development — use devtools::load_all() load_all() reads the package source directly; no .rdb is ever written, so the corruption literally cannot happen. devtools::load_all("scminerViewer") # Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + L in RStudio This is what 90% of R package developers use day-to-day. library() is for end-users. 2. RStudio: tick “Restart R prior to install” Tools → Project Options… → Build Tools → Restart R prior to install and clean — then Build → Install Package (Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + B) kills the R session before each install. Costs you the session state, but guarantees a clean .rdb. 3. Use the shipped safe-install helper for scripted installs scminerViewer/inst/scripts/install.R unloads the namespace, GCs to release mmap pages, wipes the install dir, then installs in a fresh callr subprocess — so the parent R never holds a stale handle. source(system.file("scripts", "install.R", package = "scminerViewer")) safe_install("scminerViewer") # auto-detects .libPaths()[1] safe_install("scminerViewer", lib = "/path/to/lib") Or from a shell: Rscript scminerViewer/inst/scripts/install.R scminerViewer The helper cannot unload the package from other R sessions on the same machine — those have to quit on their own first. Last resort: manual cleanup If everything’s stuck: Quit every R session that has the package loaded — in RStudio use Session → Quit Session / Cmd/Ctrl + Q. (Restarting alone isn’t enough; the OS still has the old .rdb mmap’d until the process exits.) Wipe the install directory from a shell: rm -rf "$HOME/StJude/Research/R_lib/scMINERViewer/scminerViewer" Reinstall from a fresh R session. meta.csv not found: data/<sid>/expression_files/<sid>/meta.csv The bundle resolved its shard_dir to its parent directory but the shards live somewhere else. Either move the shards into the bundle’s parent: mv data/example/expression_files data/2327/ mv data/example/activity_files data/2327/ …or tell the app where they are at launch time: run_app("data/2327/2327.scminer.h5", shard_dir = "data/example", port = 8000) run_browser("data", shard_dir = "data/example", port = 8000) scminer-viewer run data/2327/2327.scminer.h5 --shard-dir data/example scminer-viewer browse data --shard-dir data/example No documentation for 'prepare_study' The package was installed without man pages. Regenerate via roxygen2: roxygen2::roxygenise("scminerViewer") # writes NAMESPACE + man/*.Rd …then reinstall. could not find function "%>%" Older versions of the package used magrittr’s pipe in plot helpers without importing magrittr. The current version uses base R 4.1+ |> throughout, so reinstall to get the fix. Plotly “No trace type specified … Setting the mode to markers” These warnings used to come from plotly::plotly_empty() placeholders. The current version uses an explicit empty scatter trace (.empty_plot()) and the warnings should be gone — if they still appear, reinstall. run_browser shows no studies Run discover_studies(root) from R (or scminer-viewer list <root> in Python) to see what the browser would find. Each study must: be in its own subfolder named exactly the studyID, and contain a file named <studyID>.scminer.h5 (matching the folder name). A study folder produced before the multi-study refactor sits flat under the root (<root>/Cell/, <root>/Gene/, etc.); it must be wrapped in <root>/<studyID>/ to be picked up. The build_2327_bundle.R script does this automatically. A gene I expect is missing from the picker The picker is populated from the bundle’s genes/symbol group, which is the master gene list (every gene in the study, regardless of which matrices have shards). If a gene is missing here, regenerate the bundle. If a gene is in the picker but gene_values() returns NULL for a particular relationship, the gene isn’t in that matrix’s index — check study$expression_index / $activity_tf_index / $activity_sig_index (R) or study.expression_index etc. (Python). Activity matrices typically have a smaller index than expression (only TFs / SIGs are computed). Bundle is huge (>1 GB) The bundle format (bundleVersion == 1) stores indexes only — no matrix values — so a healthy .scminer.h5 is tens of MB even for studies with hundreds of thousands of cells. A multi-GB bundle is almost always an artifact written by an older non-lazy tool that inlined the expression matrix into HDF5 directly. Rebuild via prepare_study(config_path) (Chapter 3); the lazy writer drops the matrix values onto disk as per-gene gzipped CSVs under expression_files/<studyID>/ and activity_files/<studyID>/. A specific cluster disappears with sampling on The per-cluster proportional sampling keeps at least one cell per cluster (max(1L, round(n * pct / 100))) so no cluster vanishes entirely. If you see an empty cluster, the cluster has zero cells in the underlying study — check study$clusters$count (R) / study.clusters['count'] (Python). Error: attempt to construct sparseMatrix with more than 2^31-1 nonzero entries R’s Matrix::sparseMatrix() caps dgCMatrix at .Machine$integer.max non-zero entries (~2.15 billion). On a single study this only matters if the actual non-zero count of exprs(expression_eset) exceeds that limit. A 30 k-gene × 650 k-cell matrix at 100 % density has 1.95 × 10¹⁰ entries — far over the cap; the same shape at 5 % density has under 10⁹ and is fine. Two layers protect against this in the portal benchmark: scminerViewer is already row-streaming. extract_expression() and extract_activity() no longer cast the source matrix to dgCMatrix. The shard writer (.write_graph_shards) iterates genes one at a time and never materializes a full sparse copy, so it works on dense (dgeMatrix, base matrix) and sparse (dgCMatrix) inputs alike. portal_studies.R reports actual nnz but no longer pre-emptively skips. It still counts non-zero entries on load (length(m@x) if sparse, sum(m != 0) if dense) and prints a warning if the value exceeds the cap. The run is allowed to proceed because the shard writer streams genes; if .reindex_rows() then fails on a huge activity matrix downstream, the run-loop’s tryCatch tags the row as status = "error-too-large". The bsub task still exits 0 either way so the job-array merge dependency fires. If you hit this error from your own pipeline (not through portal_studies.R): Confirm exprs(eset) is sparse — class(exprs(e)) should report "dgCMatrix" or "dgeMatrix", not just "matrix". A dense base matrix gets re-allocated when any downstream code casts it. Avoid as.matrix(big_eset) or methods::as(..., "CsparseMatrix") on huge inputs; iterate by row instead. If your data genuinely has > 2³¹ nnz, you need a different storage backend (HDF5Array, BPCells, or your own gene-by-gene shard pipeline). scminerViewer’s bundle format already supports this in spirit — the shard tree is per-gene, no single sparse matrix is ever required at rest.
